Aoi, a clumsy first-year student, woke u.expanded_prompt:
Aoi Fujimura’s morning began the way most of her mornings did: in chaos. She shot upright in bed, hair tangled like seaweed, and stared at her alarm clock in horror. She was late—again. There was only one solution: grab toast, shove it in her mouth, sprint, and pray that physics would grant her five extra minutes she didn’t have.

She zoomed down the hill toward Sakura High, blazer half-buttoned, socks mismatched. Students stared. Cars honked. Aoi did not slow down.

That was when she noticed it—a tiny glowing cat, trotting alongside her shadow.

At first, she dismissed it as a trick of the sun. Her day had been neutral so far, ordinary in its disaster. But the cat kept pace with her, weaving through bicycles and schoolbags with unnatural grace.

Finally, Aoi hissed through her toast, "Shoo! I don’t have time for magical weirdness today!"

That was when the cat projected a floating hologram, shimmering like heat on summer asphalt.

HELP ME. YOU ARE THE ONLY ONE WHO CAN.

Aoi stumbled backward with a yelp. Her toast flew. Her bag flew. And then she flew, tripping over absolutely nothing, which was her signature move.

Her flailing hand smacked the glowing symbol on the cat’s collar.

The world split open.

CHAPTER 1 — Entering the Ruins
Fortune: neutral → high

A circular portal bloomed beneath her feet, swallowing her like a dropped coin. Aoi landed face-first on cracked pavement—definitely not the school entrance.

She pushed herself up and gaped.

A ruined city stretched around her, lit by amber skies and dust-swirled wind. Broken towers leaned like tired giants. Vines crawled over rusted rail lines. Yet somehow, the air hummed with energy.

People emerged from doorways—wary, yet knowing. They whispered her name: "The Chosen Returner… she’s arrived again."

Aoi blinked. Again? But before panic could bloom, her fortune shifted. Luck slipped into her palms like warm sand.

A group of guards escorted her to their camp, not as a prisoner but as an honored guest. The glowing cat—still nameless, still smug—sat on her shoulder like it had always belonged there.

By evening, she agreed—reluctantly, confusedly—to help.

"But I have a math exam!" she shouted into the twilight. The cat only blinked.

CHAPTER 2 — Days of Rising Triumph
Fortune: high → sustained high

Aoi quickly discovered something strange: everything in this broken world adored her.

Doors opened when she approached. People bowed. Technologies long dead flickered back to life at her touch. Her clumsiness remained, but instead of causing disaster, her mishaps triggered absurdly positive outcomes.

She tripped on a vine → exposed a hidden power supply the city desperately needed.
She fell through a flimsy roof → landed on a long-lost artifact no one had ever been able to find.
She sneezed near a dormant sentinel → it rebooted, recognized her, and swore loyalty.

Word spread: Aoi, the Returner, was restoring the city.

The glowing cat—who introduced himself as Hinode—began to trust her.

"You were here once," he explained. "Long ago. In another cycle."

Aoi didn’t understand, but her confidence grew. She helped rebuild shelters, activated safety grids, and even mediated disputes—mostly by accident, but somehow it all worked.

Every sunset glowed a little brighter. Every night she fell asleep thinking:

Maybe I really can save this world… and still make it back in time.

CHAPTER 3 — The Turn of Fate
Fortune: high → neutral → low

But fortune is a fickle wheel.

The twelfth day dawned with an eerie stillness.

Machines stopped responding to her touch. Doors jammed. Her jokes no longer charmed anyone. Her mishaps became real disasters.

She tripped on a loose stone → triggering a cave-in that halted repair work.
She tried to fix a beacon → overcharged it and caused a blackout.
She spilled soup on a faction leader → reigniting conflict.

People whispered now in frustration.

"Maybe she isn’t the Returner…"
"Maybe she’s a fake."

Aoi felt the sting deeply. She had never wanted to be a hero. She only wanted to do the right thing—and get back for her exam.

Hinode stayed close, but even he looked troubled.

For the first time since arriving, Aoi cried beneath the broken moon.

"What if I really can’t help anyone?" she whispered.

Hinode pressed his tiny head against her hand.

"Your fortune is a tide, Aoi. Ebbing does not mean ending."

CHAPTER 4 — The Lowest Point
Fortune: low → neutral

Disaster struck swiftly.

A sinkhole opened beneath the central district, threatening power lines Aoi had helped restore.

She ran to warn workers but slipped—falling hard and breaking a critical stabilizer.

The city trembled. People shouted in fear:

"Aoi caused this!"
"Get her away!"
"We trusted her!"

She ran until she reached the thin edge of the ruins, where portal sigils hummed like distant bells.

Hinode approached softly.

"Aoi, your time here is near its pivot. Who do you want to be?"

"My luck chooses everything for me," she said bitterly.

Hinode shook his head. "Fortune reveals your path. You decide where to step."

Aoi felt something inside steady. Her fortune returned to neutral.

CHAPTER 5 — Resurgence of the Returner
Fortune: neutral → high → sustained high

Aoi stood, dusted herself off, and marched back toward the collapsing district.

She wasn’t lucky.
She wasn’t chosen.
She wasn’t mythical.

She was Aoi—clumsy, stubborn, late for everything, including destiny, but not a quitter.

This time, she acted with intention:

She used her school engineering notes to stabilize the structure.
She coordinated citizens with newfound authority.
She used Hinode’s portal-light to activate buried circuits—deliberately.

Her fortune surged, not as random blessing, but as earned momentum.

The city brightened. People cheered her name.

A final ripple of high fortune opened a glowing gateway.

"It is time to return," Hinode said.

EPILOGUE — Back to the Exam

Aoi stumbled out of the portal and landed face-first on Sakura High’s steps.

She checked her watch.

Five minutes before the exam.

She whooped, sprinted inside, and burst into class.

"Aoi," the teacher sighed, "you’re late."

"For once," she grinned, "I think I arrived exactly when I needed to."

Hinode’s glow pulsed faintly from her pocket.

The bell rang.

Her exam began.

Her story, however, was only getting started.
